results.question: Tell me about the AI assistant on his portfolio.
results.answer: Sreehari built a generative‑AI portfolio assistant that runs on his personal website. It uses Retrieval‑Augmented Generation: his resume and project notes are split into chunks, embedded with an open‑source model, and the most relevant pieces are retrieved for each query. The system then passes those chunks to a language model that answers strictly from that context, with guardrails that block off‑topic questions, resist prompt injection, and enforce rate limits. The assistant is hosted on free‑tier services and can be accessed at https://sreeharisuresh.vercel.app.

results.question: Tell me about his traffic signal project.
results.answer: Sreehari built an Intelligent Traffic Signal Control system that uses computer‑vision techniques to count vehicles per lane from live video. The prototype employs YOLO and OpenCV in Python to detect vehicles, achieving 98% detection accuracy in controlled tests, and dynamically adjusts signal timing to prioritize high‑volume lanes while still guaranteeing a minimum wait time for every lane.

results.question: How does his currency authentication project work?
results.answer: Sreehari’s Currency Authentication project verifies Indian banknotes by first extracting security‑feature keypoints with the ORB (Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF) algorithm. It then compares these keypoints using the Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) to assess how closely the captured note matches a reference image. The combination of ORB‑based feature matching and SSIM scoring enables the system to detect counterfeit notes with about 94 % accuracy.
